newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Australia to send special envoy to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Australia to send special envoy to Cambodia.

text.p: Australia is to send a special envoy to Cambodia, Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Monday, citing "disturbing" developments in the Southeast Asian nation.
Downer told reporters in Hong Kong, where he was due to attend the handover of the British colony to China later in the day, that he also intended to visit Cambodia, perhaps in August.
"What we want to make sure is that a country which has such a tortured history but which has been delivered out of that agony enjoys political stability," he said.
In a statement, Downer said John Dauth, First Assistant Secretary of the South and Southeast Asian Division in the Foreign Ministry, would travel to Phnom Penh on July 6.
He said the decision was made in view of "recent disturbing developments", and that Dauth would "convey Australian government concerns to the highest levels of government there".
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright last week cancelled a planned trip to Phnom Penh because of security concerns.
Two envoys from the Group of Seven industrialised nations and Russia held talks last week with Cambodian leaders to raise group concerns over political stability.
The ambassadors called for an end to the violence and political instability that threatens the fragile peace established since U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
The Khmer Rouge guerrilla group appears to be disintegrating, leaving an uneasy power vacuum.
Two weeks ago, bodyguards loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen battled each other in the streets of the capital.
On Monday, Hun Sen warned that he would use force against his political opponents if they were found to be bringing troops into Phnom Penh illegally to increase their strength.
The warning came as officials loyal to Hun Sen and those loyal to Ranariddh traded accusations of clandestine troop build-ups in and around the capital.
